system.effect: When you fail a Persuasion roll, reroll it once. You said it better the second time.
Before a social encounter, ask the ST one thing the NPC actually wants. They answer honestly.
Once per scene, when the crew does something that would raise the Alert by 1, talk that single point away. Stops a +1 only — never a +2 or higher. Not an undo button for the loud mistakes.
Distract any NPC as a free action, no roll, once per scene. It holds for exactly one round.
Once per heist, after a plan visibly falls apart, declare it was the plan. The crew gets +1 die on their next roll as everyone commits to the lie.
You've been here before. You know one true detail about the target or location that wasn't in the briefing.
Leave a near-invisible line anywhere you've been. Crew can follow it or ride it as a zip line. Holds two spiders.
Stash a small item anywhere during Planning, no roll. You know exactly where it is. Nobody else does.
Reduce the Difficulty of Stealth rolls made while moving by 1. You don't make noise. You make a point of it.
Climb any surface at full Speed with no roll — even slick or hostile ones that would cost other spiders double or a check.
When you're the one spotted, immediately make a free Stealth roll to vanish again before the NPC reacts.
Increase the Difficulty for any NPC to remember seeing you by 2. You are deeply, fundamentally forgettable.
Once per scene, fix, jam, or modify a small mechanical device with a Difficulty 2 Engineering roll. Locks, sensors, that one drawer.
Spend a turn observing an area and the ST tells you whether any mechanical traps, alarms, or sensors are present — not where.
Spend 1 Silk Point for +2 dice on an Engineering roll. It just takes more legs than usual.
Once per scene, patch an adjacent crewmate's Vitality up one level with a Difficulty 2 Engineering roll. You're an engineer, not a doctor. Close enough.
During Planning, set one web-based trap on the known map. When an NPC triggers it, the ST rolls Difficulty 3 for them to avoid it.
The first time you meet any new lock, alarm, or mechanism, ask the ST one yes/no question about how it works. Free. Just by looking.
Once per scene, redirect a physical consequence meant for an adjacent crewmate to yourself. You chose this.
Ignore the first -1 die penalty from being Rattled. You've been Rattled before. You're fine.
Enter a scene from an unexpected direction and every NPC must pass a Difficulty 3 check or freeze in surprise for a round.
Your presence helps. The Face gets +1 die on Persuasion while you're visibly nearby.
Fire a silk line to grab and restrain a target up to 3 squares away — Brawl, Difficulty 3. Small targets held one round.
After a hit that would drop you to Critical, roll Endurance (Difficulty 3). On a success, you stop at Hurt instead.
At the start of each obstacle, the ST tells you which direction any active threat moves next. No roll.
Once per round, give a crewmate +1 die on their next roll by telling them exactly what to do. You're not helping. You're instructing.
After watching a patrol or recurring threat for one full round, you know its next three actions.
Once per heist during Planning, set one Contingency with the ST. If a specific trigger happens, it activates automatically as a success.
You always know the fastest way out of a room you've been in. Reduce the Difficulty of escape rolls by 1 while you lead.
Detect when an NPC is watching a specific area — Perception, Difficulty 2. On a success, the ST tells you what's watched and from where.
You can't be fully cornered. Even when the ST would logically have you trapped, you have one option left. It may be unpleasant.
During Planning, establish one shortcut between two points on the known map. The crew can use it once.
Remove the penalty from height-based Acrobatics rolls. You've looked down. You've made your peace.
Carry one incapacitated crewmate at full Speed. It looks extremely dramatic.
When you lead group movement, each crewmate gets +1 die on movement rolls. You set the pace; they follow.
Once per heist, call an immediate abort on a failed plan. The crew retreats without the extra Alert that failure would have added.
Choose one NPC before the heist; you've studied them. +2 dice on all Deception and Disguise involving that NPC.
When an NPC sees through your disguise, reveal the disguise was the distraction. Spend 1 Silk Point; the NPC is confused for a round.
During Planning, place one false piece of information on the known map. The first NPC to find it believes it completely.
Alter your disguise between scenes with no roll. You look different now. You are still a spider.
Spend Planning establishing a false identity and all rolls using it get +1 die. The identity must be specific and named.
When you fail a Deception roll, reframe the failure as intentional. The NPC still isn't fooled, but they don't raise the Alert.
